title: RPi Metrics Bridge
description: Homelab Pi 5 dashboard fed by the rpi-metrics-bridge Prometheus textfile collector (rpi-health, host-health, rpi-cooling, rpi-rtc, rpi-pcie, rpi-boot-config, rpi-connect, rpi-gpio-inventory, rpi-camera, apt-inventory).

panels.title: Capture Age by Source
panels.description: Seconds since each source's last successful capture. Should hover near 0-60s; a rising line means that source's collect step is failing.

panels.title: Bridge Export Freshness
panels.description: Seconds since rpi_metrics.prom was last written by the timer. Alert if > 300.

panels.title: Textfile Scrape Error
panels.description: 1 if node_exporter failed to parse any textfile collector file (malformed write, permissions, etc).

panels.title: SoC / Filesystem Temperature
panels.description: CPU/SoC core temperature vs. the hottest thermal zone reported by the kernel (may be the same sensor, or a different one on some boards).

panels.title: Core / Supply Voltage
panels.description: SoC core voltage and the 5V rail voltage as reported by vcgencmd — a sagging supply rail under load points at a power-delivery problem before it causes visible instability.

panels.title: Estimated Total Power Draw
panels.description: host-health's estimate of whole-board power draw in watts, derived from voltage/current readings — not a certified measurement, but useful for spotting trend changes (e.g. after attaching new hardware).

panels.title: ARM Clock Speed
panels.description: Current ARM core frequency. A sudden drop usually means thermal or under-voltage throttling kicked in — cross-check against the Sticky Fault Bits and SoC Temperature panels.

panels.title: Sticky Fault Bits (since boot)
panels.description: 1 = fault occurred at some point since boot, even if not currently active. healthy=0 means at least one sticky bit is set.

panels.title: Fan RPM
panels.description: Measured fan speed from the case's tachometer feedback pin, if wired. Compare against Fan PWM Duty Cycle — RPM not tracking a duty cycle change is what Fan Stalled is watching for.

panels.title: Fan PWM Duty Cycle
panels.description: Commanded fan speed as a percentage (0-100), set by the thermal governor based on Cooling State — this is the target, not the measured result (see Fan RPM for that).

panels.title: Cooling State
panels.description: Current cooling-device state vs. its max state (thermal governor step level, not a temperature).

panels.title: Fan Stalled
panels.description: Kernel-detected stall: the fan is commanded to spin (nonzero PWM duty cycle) but its tachometer isn't reporting rotation. STALLED here means physically check the fan, not a software issue.

panels.title: Disk Usage
panels.description: Root filesystem usage vs. the single worst-utilized mount on the host — the worst mount is what actually triggers 'disk full' problems, since it may not be root.

panels.title: Memory Used
panels.description: RAM used as a percentage of total. Sustained near-100% usage is what drives swap usage up (see Swap Used) and eventually the OOM killer.

panels.title: Swap Used
panels.description: Bytes of zram swap in use (this machine uses compressed RAM-backed swap, not a swap partition — see MIGRATION.md). Rising swap usage alongside high Memory Used means the workload has outgrown RAM.

panels.title: Load Average
panels.description: Standard Unix load averages (1/5/15 min) — number of runnable+uninterruptible processes on average. Compare against Load5 per Core to judge whether a given number is actually high for this machine's core count.

panels.title: Load5 per Core
panels.description: 5-minute load average divided by core count — normalizes Load Average so 1.0 means 'fully using every core,' comparable across machines with different core counts.

panels.title: Process Counts
panels.description: Total process/thread count vs. how many are currently runnable (ready to run but waiting for CPU). A runnable count that tracks total procs closely means CPU contention, not just many idle processes.

panels.title: Upgradable Packages
panels.description: Total packages apt would upgrade right now vs. how many of those are classified security-relevant by apt's own origin string. Any nonzero security count is worth acting on soon.

panels.title: Installed Packages
panels.description: Total currently-installed dpkg packages on the host. Mostly useful as a trend line — a sudden jump usually means a manual install or a big dependency pull.

panels.title: Vulnerability Scan (debsecan)
panels.description: Total CVE/package entries debsecan reports, split into actionable (real, currently-fixable — the number that matters) and false positive (already patched, per dpkg's own version comparison — see apt-inventory's actuallyFixed logic).

panels.title: PCIe / RTC / Connect
panels.description: PCIe link degraded: yes is bad (red). RTC synced / Connect signed in: yes is good (green) — each field has its own mapping since 'yes' means something different per metric.

panels.title: RTC Drift
panels.description: System clock minus the hardware RTC's own clock, in seconds. A few seconds is normal drift between syncs; anything growing into minutes means the RTC battery or chip needs attention.

panels.title: GPIO / Camera
panels.description: GPIO pin count from gpiochip0, plus CSI camera detection. 'camera recognized' means rpicam-hello's output matched a known format (zero cameras is a valid, recognized result on this hardware) — NO means the parser hit unrecognized output and needs a look.

panels.title: Boot Config Change-Hash
panels.description: Opaque content hash for change-detection, not a magnitude to read — it only matters whether this value changes run to run, so it's shown at full width to avoid clipping and colored neutrally (not by size).

panels.title: Core Extension Run Log
panels.description: Live journald output from the ops repo's swamp serve (user unit swamp-serve.service in rpi-metrics-bridge, which runs every scheduled workflow) via Loki/Promtail, for every workflow not on the Fun Stuff dashboard. Promtail lifts the workflow name into a `workflow` label. Serve logs one line per scheduled fire, start and outcome (completed, or failed with the assert message); per-step output stays in swamp's own run history (`swamp workflow history`).

panels.title: Units Monitored
panels.description: Units with a trustworthy pass/fail signal, out of the total checked, from the fleet-health repo's health-check workflow (runs every 5 minutes).

panels.title: Stale Exports
panels.description: Prometheus textfile exports currently beyond their own expected freshness window. 0 is healthy.

panels.title: New Errors (10m)
panels.description: New error-level log lines in the last 10 minutes, excluding already-tracked baseline noise (PCIe link-integrity, rpi-connect's expected not-signed-in, iss-tracker's occasional flaky public-API fetch). 0 is healthy.

panels.title: Fleet Health Check Freshness
panels.description: Seconds since fleet-health.prom was last written by its 10-minute timer. Alert if this climbs well past ~20 minutes.

panels.title: Per-Unit Status
panels.description: 1 = last recognized run succeeded, 0 = failed. A unit missing from this table has no trustworthy signal (see Units Monitored) — check it manually.

panels.title: Critical Warning
panels.description: NVMe critical_warning byte. 0 is healthy; anything else (spare low, over temperature, reliability degraded, read-only) means back up the drive. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: Available Spare
panels.description: Remaining spare capacity. The drive raises critical_warning below its own threshold (10% here); @aaronge/nvme-health fails 5 points earlier. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: Wear Used
panels.description: Vendor estimate of rated endurance used. @aaronge/nvme-health fails at 80%. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: Media Errors
panels.description: Lifetime unrecovered data-integrity errors. Any is bad; @aaronge/nvme-health fails on each new one. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: Unsafe Shutdowns
panels.description: Lifetime power losses without a clean shutdown. A rise is a power witness (also checked by power-integrity), not a drive fault. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: Power-On Hours
panels.description: Lifetime powered-on hours. Debian's prometheus-node-exporter-collectors nvme.prom (every 15 minutes). The @aaronge/nvme-health workflow asserts on the same data from the ops serve.

panels.title: NVMe Temperatures
panels.description: Every hwmon sensor on the drive, from @aaronge/nvme-health's readTemperature (metrics-export, every 5 minutes). The drive's own warning threshold is 85°C; @aaronge/nvme-health fails at 70°C.

panels.title: NVMe Throughput
panels.description: Host read and write rates from the drive's own data-unit counters (1 unit = 512,000 bytes), averaged over 30 minutes. Sustained high writes eat into rated endurance.

panels.title: Thermal Throttling
panels.description: Seconds the drive has spent thermally throttled (light = TMT1, heavy = TMT2), from @aaronge/nvme-health. Not in Debian's nvme.prom.

panels.title: Minutes Over Temperature
panels.description: Minutes above the drive's own warning and critical composite thresholds, from @aaronge/nvme-health. Not in Debian's nvme.prom.
